principle: Publish the best defensible reconstruction of where the activity actually occurred, rather than automatically preferring the rawest or densest GPS representation.
sourcePreservation: Preserve original GPX/FIT evidence internally even when the published geometry is filtered, corrected, or reconstructed.
distanceReference: Strava activity distance is a strong sanity check, not a hard optimization target.
selectionRules: Prefer spatial and path truth over raw point count.
Use the least destructive correction that removes implausible GPS behavior while preserving genuine turns and route detail.
Use distance agreement to validate a candidate, not to choose it mechanically.
Reconstruct missing geometry from external trail, road, course, timing, photo, or itinerary evidence when a plausible path can be defended.
When several reconstructions remain plausible, select the most plausible path and mark it as inferred rather than disguising it as recorded GPS.
Never silently convert inferred geometry into recorded geometry.

inferredRendering.readerFacingDetail: Keep explanatory metadata minimal; the dash itself communicates that the segment is inferred.

legacyCompatibility: Existing route-detail quality floors continue to protect technical route detail during migration. Geometry class and explicit publication selection determine fidelity independently of point density.
